requirements.text: Validate schema and quarantine ambiguous identity without guessing.
Bind approval to an immutable entity/revision and serialize accepted revisions.
Deduplicate events and retain decision provenance through retries.

problem.scope: Deidentified authored records exercise schema validation, identity resolution, ordered approval and idempotent commit. This is an ingestion pattern with no patient data, clinical rules or clinical decisions.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Transactions isolate concurrent authorization and mutation decisions; retries remain explicit.
references.title: PostgreSQL isolation

acceptanceCases.given: One event fails the pinned schema and another names an identity hint matching two entities.

acceptanceCases.then: The decision log keeps the superseded hash-A approval and the committed hash-B decision with actor, policy version and source receipt.

guarantees: Validation failure cannot become accepted data.

stages.explanation: Validate schema and quarantine ambiguous identity without guessing. Admission stores the payload hash under its eventId; nothing commits until a bound approval names that entity, revision and hash. [Data ingestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_integration) moves source records into a usable destination. Stable source identity and progress records distinguish genuinely new data from repeated delivery or a restarted import.
invariants: Admission stores the payload hash under its eventId; nothing commits until a bound approval names that entity, revision and hash.

stages.explanation: Validate event envelopes before accepting workflow intent. Own immutable raw event hashes and revision state. The staging ledger is the single writer of event receipts and entity revisions; the coordinator reads and updates them in one transaction. [Immutable data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immutable_object) is built as a complete new value rather than changed underneath readers. Publishing one reference lets each reader keep a consistent version.

[Idempotence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idempotence) means repeating the same logical operation does not repeat its effect. Stable request identities let a retry recover an existing outcome instead of creating another change.

acceptanceCases.given: An approval arrives before its matching event.
acceptanceCases.then: Keep it unbound; no accepted record appears.
acceptanceCases.when: Replay with a mismatched payload hash.

acceptanceCases.given: A partition consumer replays a committed event.
acceptanceCases.when: Apply the event and checkpoint again.

acceptanceCases.given: An envelope's identity hint matches two entities at the current mapping version.
acceptanceCases.then: It enters the quarantine queue with its candidates; no entity partition receives it.

acceptanceCases.given: A repaired identity mapping v2 would assign an old event to a different entity.
acceptanceCases.then: The active projection keeps the v1 decision until the v2 generation is explicitly published; history is not edited in place.
acceptanceCases.when: Build and compare a new projection generation.

evidence.testName: L028 entity-log reducer keeps pending events and approvals without blocking the partition

acceptanceCases.given: One partition carries entity X revision 1 without approval, entity Y revision 1 with its approval, an early approval for X revision 2, a wrong-hash approval and then the right approval for X revision 1.
acceptanceCases.then: Y applies while X waits; the wrong hash stays unbound; X revision 1 applies on its approval and revision 2 as soon as its event arrives; offsets advance on every record and replays change nothing.
acceptanceCases.when: Reduce the records in offset order, then replay a checkpointed offset and a duplicate event.

guarantees: Unresolved identity has no accepted entity partition.
Replay uses the original mapping version.
An approval is a partition record, never a commit by itself; it binds only an event with the same entity, revision and hash.
Offsets advance on every record together with reducer state, including pending events and approvals; a missing approval never blocks other entities.
Replay is idempotent for accepted revisions.
A new mapping cannot mutate historic decisions in place.
